items.title: "Kid Thomas" Valentine Interview, 1959-12-10
items.q: The interviewee addresses 'Mr. Bin' directly ('I tell you Mr. Bin', 'You hear me for doing business... Mr. Bin'), indicating a personal acquaintance or relationship, but no specific professional or close personal bond (like friend, mentor, or collaborator) is described in the text regarding Mr. Bin

ctx.x: On the race. Went in places, one of the horses was Banjo, they were just talking about it. Shut up. Putting the name up. Yeah, so he said whatever he pawned his banjo for, twenty dollars or something, put twenty dollars on banjo. He'd never heard of the horse. I know, sure. And he won right there.

He won. Just because it was his banjo. Well sure, that was just luck. I mean, there's a lot of luck there sometimes. It's not luck. You see, I tell you Mr. Bin, now you hear a lot of people say about luck. You take like this man's pick. That's the luckiest man in dancing, you know what I mean? I mean for business, you know what I mean? He was a lucky man for that, you see? And he, him and a colored fella had a place there over there in Walkerstown, you see?
